blocks.content: I have a theory that mornings belong to whoever shows up for them. Iced coffee before breakfast, mismatched socks because they make me smile, the long way through town because the sky was doing something worth looking at. That's my version of intentional.
My phone buzzed before I'd made it half a block.
I flipped it face-down and took a very deliberate sip of my coffee.

The arcade on Clement smelled like carpet and sugar and someone's optimistic 2003, which is exactly how it should smell. Lena was already inside, keys in hand, giving me the look she gives me when I show up before something opens.
She rolled her eyes and unlocked the door. That's the thing about Lena — she acts immovable and then moves every single time for the people she loves. I'm still figuring out how to do it back.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: She asked if you took it.
I turned toward the claw machine and pretended to study the options.
There's this thing that happens when someone who loves you is also right. The irritation has nowhere to go. It just sits in your chest being inconvenient.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I just want today to feel normal.
No lecture. Just okay. I love her so much for that.
I beat the claw machine on the third try. The purple dinosaur was enormous and slightly lopsided and I held him over my head like I'd won something that actually mattered.
She didn't smile, but the corner of her mouth did something. That's good enough for me.
I named him Winston because he had the face of something that had been through things and wasn't making a big deal about it.
